newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria FIS leader expected to be freed after trial.
newsitem.headline: Algeria FIS leader expected to be freed after trial.

text.p: Algerian authorities were expected on Tuesday to release Abdelkader Hachani, the once-powerful leader of the Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) sentenced to five years in prison by a court on Monday.

The official Algerian news agency APS said: "According to a source close to the public prosecutor's office, the application of this sentence takes effect counting from the date the accused was taken into detention."

Hachani had been held in Sirkadji high security prison in Algiers since January 22, 1992 -- nearly six months longer than the sentence passed late on Monday by Algiers criminal court on charges of seeking to undermine state security.
The state prosecutor had asked the court to jail him for 10 years. The court stripped Hachani of his civil rights for a period of three years.

Earlier this month, the FIS executive in exile called on the Algerians to free Hachani, saying: "This would certainly contribute to an easing of tensions required to promote the necessary climate for a return to peace and stability."
The Algerian newspaper Liberte also said on Tuesday: "Having already purged the total of the jail sentence in preventative detention, Abdelkader Hachani will come out of prison today."

On Monday, Hachani, who led the FIS to a landslide victory in Algeria's first mutli-party general election -- only to see it vanish as the authorities in January 1992 scrapped the poll -- heard the state prosecutor tell the court he bore "entire responsibility for the events through which Algeria has lived".
About 60,000 people have been killed in violence that erupted shortly after the ballot was scrapped. Much of the country of 29 million still lives in the shadow of bloodshed.
Hachani, a former oil engineer, was charged with trying to undermine state security just after the December 1991 first round of the election was cancelled.
The charges arose from a statement in his name which appeared in al-Khabar newspaper, urging Algerian soldiers to disobey their officers and not to strike at Islamist activists.
The Defence Ministry accused him of "launching an appeal for rebellion in the army" and on January 22, 1992, he was arrested.
Hachani, now aged about 40, told the trial judges: "The aim of the appeal was to avoid confrontation and involvement of the ANP (army) in political struggles."

His defence team, headed by Ali Yahia Abdennour, leader of an independent Algerian human rights group, and Mustapha Bouchachi, asked the court to release him in view of the time he had been in custody.

Viewed as a relative moderate who had urged FIS activists to avoid violence, Hachani in 1992 termed the cancellation of the poll "a coup d'etat against the Islamic state" which the FIS planned for the North African country.
Under his provisional leadership, with the party's two top men already in detention, the FIS had won 188 of the 232 seats decided outright in the first round.

Algeria last month held the first multi-party general election since the 1992 poll cancellation. Radical Islamists were barred but two moderate Islamist parties were allowed to compete. They won a total of 103 seats in the 380-seat National Assembly.
